verdict.rationale: Hatchet documents per-key concurrency limits defined with CEL expressions, including tiered limits per user and shared concurrency rules. This keeps any one tenant or user from monopolizing execution, a form of fairness beyond a single FIFO queue. The pack has no evidence of assigning priorities to runs, and it never describes a fair-scheduling algorithm (such as round-robin across tenants) as such. missing for 10: run-level priority assignment, explicit fair/round-robin scheduling across tenants, independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I assign priorities to runs and get fair scheduling across tenants instead of a single FIFO queue

citations.quote: set concurrency limits on a per-key basis using a CEL expression. For example, let premium-tier users run 10 workflows simultaneously while other users run one
create concurrency rules that many tasks and workflows consume simultaneously, e.g. limiting `workflow_a` and `workflow_b` to 10 concurrent runs per user total
configure the queue depth for each concurrency key
